slides.title:
Poison-resilient
continual NIDS
slides.subtitle: A tabular Transformer research prototype
slides.question: Can a model learn new attack classes, retain prior knowledge and tolerate corrupted update labels?
slides.footer: Bounded experiments completed. Full clean training in progress.
slides.notes: Research objective, not an achieved robustness claim. NIDS means Network Intrusion Detection System. The prototype combines a custom tabular Transformer, two-task class expansion, replay, label corruption, a frozen-teacher gate and confidence novelty. All objectives are evaluated separately. No pretrained model, deployment readiness or literature superiority is claimed. Current run status comes from the user, not a completed test artifact.

slides.callout:
Combined flow collection
Per-row source provenance is unavailable.
slides.notes: The local Parquet has 59 columns: 57 numeric features plus Label and ClassLabel. Both targets are excluded from features. The audited policy excludes Fwd Header Length, Bwd Header Length and Fwd Seg Size Min, leaving 54. Stable global IDs must match model probability columns. Do not attribute this collection to a particular CIC year without provenance. Counts and mapping are supported by the actual split_manifest.json inspected for this presentation and the repository audit.

slides.title: Train-only preprocessing and split protocol
steps:
Invalid values → missing
Median fill, standardize

Same feature order
Validation and test unchanged
slides.left:
Fit using all eight training classes.
Bounded sample: 2,000 rows per class.
11,200 / 2,400 / 2,400 split rows.
slides.right:
Fit using Task 1 training classes only.
Task 2 never fits preprocessing.
Replay contains Task 1 training rows only.
slides.callout: Row-level stratification does not rule out duplicate-flow or capture-session leakage.
slides.notes: Negative and non-finite values become missing. Small-array preprocessing uses training medians, then training population means and scales after imputation. The full-data route approximates medians from a seeded 200,000-row reservoir, separately for static and continual scopes. Validation selects models or thresholds. Test is held for evaluation. Splits preserve row identity and exclude validation/test IDs from replay. Source provenance is absent, so a row split is not evidence of session isolation.

slides.title: Custom tabular Transformer
slides.left:
Cross-entropy with AdamW
Learning rate 0.001, dropout 0.1
Validation-loss checkpoint selection
slides.right:
predict_proba columns follow class_ids
Expandable output head for new classes
Saved models support reload checks
slides.callout: This is a compact custom architecture. All model weights begin with fresh initialization.
slides.notes: The implementation tokenizes each scalar x_j as x_j*w_j+b_j, adds a learned CLS token and learned position embeddings, runs pre-norm Transformer encoder layers with GELU, then classifies the CLS representation through LayerNorm, dropout and a linear head. The compact run configuration is hidden64, four heads, two layers, MLP128. These are experiment overrides, not the larger ModelConfig defaults. Full clean training uses batch256, weight_decay 0.0001, seed42, mixed precision off, maximum20 epochs, patience5. The model is not pretrained.

slides.title: Static baseline: strong average, weak Benign recall
slides.left:
16,000 sampled rows, eight classes
2,400 test rows, 300 per class
20 epochs, best validation epoch 17
slides.right:
168 of 300 Benign flows called attacks
138 of those called Infiltration
Benign recall: 44.0%
slides.callout: Aggregate accuracy does not establish reliable normal-traffic handling.
slides.notes: Actual metrics (1).json inspected in this session reports accuracy 0.8833333333333333, macro-F1 0.878016638838182 and a Benign confusion row [132,4,9,1,0,138,6,10]. Thus false positives are 300-132=168, FPR=0.56 and recall=0.44. Best epoch17 and matched checkpoint reload are documented in the walkthrough. These are single-seed balanced-subset results, not natural-distribution full-data metrics. Source run 68135601a3ddd95832c57bb602f210f1a0e18a43.

slides.title: Continual expansion and replay
steps:
Independent reloads
Expand head to IDs 0–7

New classes only
or new classes + replay
slides.callout: Memory: 500 unique old training rows, 100 per class. Old accuracy before Task 2: 96.87%.
slides.notes: Task1 includes Benign, DDoS, DoS, Botnet and Bruteforce. Task2 adds Infiltration, Webattack and Portscan. Expanded arms reload the same Task1 checkpoint and use the same expansion seed. A balanced stored memory means equal unique examples per old class; it does not mean balanced training draws. Sequential/replay used264/444 optimizer steps and8/12 epochs, so comparison is unequal-compute. Signed accuracy forgetting equals old accuracy before minus after on identical old test rows, with predictions into new classes counted as errors. Replay forgetting=28.60 percentage points. This initial continual result is supported by the repository audit record; the replay values also match the supplied test_summary.json. No new training was executed for this presentation.

slides.title: Label poisoning uses explicit budgets
slides.left:
Budget denominator: all training rows
Choose a different allowed label
20% = 2,240 / 11,200 rows
slides.right:
Denominator: eligible attack rows
Target class: Benign (ID 0)
20% = 1,960 / 9,800 eligible rows
Equivalent to 17.5% of all training rows
slides.callout: Sweep: 0%, 5%, 10%, 20%. Effects were not monotonic across all metrics.
slides.notes: Training labels only are corrupted, features and clean validation/test labels stay fixed. Count=floor(rate*eligible_count+0.5), sampling without replacement. Random selects a different label from all eight classes. Targeted sources are attack IDs1–7, target0. Actual comparison.json inspected: random20 changed2240, targeted20 changed1960. Attack-to-Benign rate is measured on true attack test rows; its clean baseline is nonzero. Random10 accuracy0.88375 and targeted10 macro-F1 0.881780487 exceeded the corresponding clean value slightly, so poisoning does not uniformly worsen every metric. Same initial weights and seven reload checks are documented. Single seed and balanced data limit inference.

slides.title: Frozen-teacher filtering has mixed outcomes
slides.callout: All simulated poison labels rejected, but random-poison accuracy fell. Benign FPR remained 90.0–95.3%.
slides.notes: Frozen teacher is the clean five-class Task1 model trained from scratch. It filters old-class replay only, never new Task2 examples. Simulator truth is used afterward for audit, never for filtering or repairing labels. Random20 budget100/500 replay rows. Targeted20 budget80/400 eligible old attack rows,16% of total replay. Clean false rejection was4.4%; random4.75%; targeted4.2857%. Actual comparison(1).json was inspected. Combined test accuracy pairs are .7804167/.81375, .81625/.7858333, .81625/.8279167. Optimizer steps differ: clean444/444, random370/648, targeted444/504, so rejection and accuracy effects cannot be isolated from training work and changed memory size. This is a narrow label-consistency baseline, not a general poisoning/backdoor defense.

slides.title: Balanced draws improve retention with tradeoffs
slides.callout: Same 500 unique replay rows. Validation selected balanced draws. Training work differed: 444 vs 370 steps.
slides.notes: Actual test_summary.json and strategy_selection.json inspected. Balanced inverse-frequency sampling uses replacement and one draw per combined row per epoch. Buffer size is unchanged; repeated exposure changes. Clean validation macro-F1 selected balanced:0.8529213667 vs0.7541214312, with no test or novelty data used for selection. Old test1500 rows, new test900, combined2400. Forgetting is before-minus-after old accuracy in percentage points; smaller is better here. This helps old retention but reduces new-class accuracy and still misclassifies61.67% of Benign examples. One seed, one balanced subset and unequal optimizer work preclude broad claims.

slides.title: Held-out novelty recall remains weak
slides.left:
Task 1 classes known, Task 2 held out
Flag unknown if max probability < 0.9248
Cutoff: fifth percentile of known validation
slides.callout: 730 of 900 unknown examples were missed. Many unseen flows still receive high confidence.
slides.notes: Actual novelty.json inspected. Threshold0.9247980117797852 calibrated on1500 known validation rows only using the fifth percentile, frozen before Task2 evaluation. Task1 known test has1500 rows, Task2 unknown test900 rows, each unknown class300. True unknown flagged170, false known rejected68, unknown missed730. Recall170/900=.1888889; precision170/(170+68)=.7142857. This evaluation occurs before the head expands and before Task2 learning. Known false rejection is a novelty metric, distinct from Benign classification FPR. Equality to the cutoff counts as known. This is genuine held-out-class evidence of a weak confidence baseline, not broad novelty robustness.

slides.notes: A local interface is planned, not implemented or built in this task. The one-command integration path is still incomplete. Proposed demo is offline inference on compatible precomputed flow features, with explicit feature order, saved preprocessing and class mapping. It should display confidence-baseline caveats and no deployment-readiness claim. Future priorities are verification of full clean test outputs, then separate full-data continual/replay and poisoning experiments; repeated seeds and provenance-aware splits would improve evidence. No team PDF, web interface or training job was created during presentation work.
